To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Solanum dulcanara callus and cell suspension tissue cultures can accumulate soladulcidin, a steroidal alkaloid, and that regenerated plants contain the same alkaloid in the same concentration as the source plant.

Solanum dulcanara callus and green cell suspension cultures accumulate solasodine, soladulcididine and tigogenine, and that the regenerated plants from mixotrophic calli contain soladulcidinine and tigogeninine.
Solanum dulcama L. is a good source of soladulcidines, and that these alkaloids can be produced in tissue cultures.

the biosynthesis of steroidal alkaloids in cell cultures of Solanum species.
